text: This lab works a full incident, end to end, using everything this chapter has covered: triage, the support decision, and a real postmortem.

At 1:50 on a Tuesday afternoon, reports start coming in from multiple departments that everything in ServiceNow is slow. Reports continue for 45 minutes, then stop around 2:35, as if it resolved on its own. This is exactly the ambiguous, platform-wide complaint Lesson 19's triage sequence was built for.

Walking the three triage steps: first, scope. The Instance Health Dashboard shows response time roughly tripling starting right at 1:50, while transaction volume stays flat — genuine degradation, not a busy-Tuesday spike. Second, deployment history. A release went out at 1:47, three minutes before the first reports, updating a Business Rule on the Incident table that runs an unindexed GlideRecord query on every single update — on a table that busy, that degrades performance for every user, instance-wide. Third, resources. Semaphore usage was elevated, but with no sign of a separate runaway job, consistent with slower transactions simply holding semaphores longer — a downstream effect of the root cause already found, not a second problem.

Now the support decision. Does this need a ServiceNow Support case? No. It's customization-caused, fully self-diagnosable, and self-fixable — disable the rule, add the missing index, redeploy. Opening a case here would have sent ServiceNow's engineers to investigate something already solved. Unexplained infrastructure capacity pressure, on the other hand, would genuinely have justified one.

Finally, the postmortem, using Lesson 21's four components in full: a timeline from the 1:47 deployment through 2:35 resolution, a specific root cause naming the unindexed query running on every Incident update, the actual fix — disabling the rule, adding an indexed filter, redeploying — and one concrete prevention action, an ATF performance-regression check added before the next release, with a named owner and a real deadline. Written blamelessly, the postmortem asks what let an unoptimized query reach production undetected, not who wrote it.
Next up: the course's own capstone begins, with a realistic slow-instance scenario you'll diagnose and fix yourself.
